name: Anya Li
life: “For a year I tasted everything on a client's plate before she would eat.” On Monday, near Juniper Street, Anya knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I squeezed the orange she carried in her pocket. Nobody knew her medicine left a bitter taste.
appearance: Anya is easy to recognize by black hair twisted into a small knot and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric, Anya gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Anya has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Anya knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To re-create the orange's bitterness in the patient's usual order.
family: Morgan Freeman is Anya’s cousin. Anya checks the date twice. Morgan brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *A widow bids again*, Morgan says, “I still have a lease written on a birthday card.”
connections: Jody Graves. They compare the mustard remembered at the counter with the orange remembered on the walk home.

reactions.situation: A relative hates the ingredient everyone remembers
reactions.response: Anya lets the relative choose a different sandwich without defending the menu.

reactions.situation: A traveler asks for the last seat at the bus stop
reactions.response: Anya gives up their own space if possible and asks the passengers who arrived first to choose what happens next.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Anya asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
